newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Nov inflation 0.47 pct vs 1.2 pct yr ago.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Nov inflation 0.47 pct vs 1.2 pct yr ago.

text.p: Consumer prices rose 0.47 percent in November, compared with a 1.2 percent rise in the same month last year and 0.73 percent in October, the government's National Institute of Information and Statistics (INEI) said Monday.
Accumulated inflation in the first eleven months of 1996 was 10.51 percent, up from 8.3 percent in the same period last year, according to INEI figures published in the official daily El Peruano.
Consumer inflation fell to 10.2 percent in 1995 from 15.4 percent the previous year. The 1995 figure was the lowest in 23 years.

Although the government originally aimed for single-digit inflation this year and agreed to a target of between 9.5 percent and 11.5 percent with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the latest official prediction for this year's inflation is 12 percent.
The government estimates next year's accumulated inflation will be nine percent and will drop to "the level of industrialized countries" by 2000.
